newsitem.title: ESTONIA: TALLINNA FARMA SET TO ENTER UKRAINE.
newsitem.headline: TALLINNA FARMA SET TO ENTER UKRAINE.

text.p: Tallinn Farma pharmaceuticals company is looking beyond its main markets in Russia to Ukraine and hopes for sales of around five million dollars, Priit Kivi, chairman of the board, told Reuters.
"Based on our maximum volume we will expect five million dollars in sales to Ukraine over 97/98," Kivi said in a recent interview.
"The total turnover to Ukraine was less than two percent of total sales, so the rise will be very big," he added.
At present 90 percent of Farma's sales are to the vast but unpredictable Russian market.
The company is already seeking to make the most of it connections with the Russian market, he added.
"We have a plant in Moscow which is aimed at packaging and not production with 30 percent of our sales in the Moscow region," Kivi added.
"Because two thirds of our employees are Russian speakers we have also found a way around the double tariffs Russia applies to imports from Estonia," he said.
"We now export on equal terms as other importers to the Russian Market."
The company will also open a new production line that matches international good management practices (GMP) standard.
"The first production from this new plant will released in June," Sven Nugis, Farma finance director, said.
